svg.title: Block ID and bank ID: one slot, two local bank histories
svg.desc: An UpdateParent marker changes the parent of slot 104 from block P in slot 103 to block Q in slot 102. The leader replaces local bank 42 with 43. A receiving validator replaces local bank 900 with 901. Both compute the same block ID H104 for the completed block. All numbers and hash names are illustrative.

g.aria-label: Slot: a position in the schedule. Show explanation
g.title: Slot: the position in the schedule. A parent change can replace a bank without changing its slot.
g.text: A slot alone does not identify a block.

g.aria-label: Block ID: shared block identity. Show explanation
g.title: Block ID: a cryptographic identity computed from the block's shreds and selected parent. Nodes with the same block compute the same ID.
g.text: Names exact block data and its parent.

g.aria-label: Bank ID: local execution instance. Show explanation
g.title: Bank ID: a local u64 counter assigned when a Bank is created. It is not a content hash and must not be compared across validators or restarts.
g.text: Each validator allocates its own IDs.

g.aria-label: Leader before UpdateParent: slot 104, bank ID 42, parent P. Show explanation
g.title: Before UpdateParent: the leader has created an optimistic Bank for slot 104 on parent P, the block in slot 103.
g.text: Child block ID is not yet available.

g.aria-label: Receiver before UpdateParent: slot 104, bank ID 900, parent P. Show explanation
g.title: In this example the receiver has already created its own optimistic Bank for slot 104. Its local bank ID is 900, not the leader's 42.
g.text: Local IDs need not match the leader.

g.aria-label: I01: the ready parent differs; emit UpdateParent. Show explanation
g.title: I01: ParentReady selects Q instead of P. The leader drains old record input and emits UpdateParent in the shred stream.
g.text: I01 · Ready parent Q differs from P

g.aria-label: UpdateParent wire marker: new parent slot 102 and new parent block ID Q. Show explanation
g.title: UpdateParent carries new_parent_slot and new_parent_block_id. It identifies a network block, not another validator's local bank. This is a block marker carried in shreds.

g.aria-label: I02: the leader creates its replacement bank. Show explanation
g.title: I02: The leader clears its optimistic Bank and creates a new Bank for the same slot on parent Q. The local bank ID changes.

g.aria-label: I03: replay creates the receiver's replacement bank. Show explanation
g.title: I03: The receiving validator applies the marker and recreates its local Bank from the matching selected parent. Parent state must be available. Its counter is independent of the leader's.

g.aria-label: Leader after UpdateParent: slot 104, bank ID 43, parent Q. Show explanation
g.title: The leader's replacement Bank still represents slot 104, but its local bank ID is now 43 and it uses parent block Q in slot 102.

g.aria-label: Receiver after UpdateParent: slot 104, bank ID 901, parent Q. Show explanation
g.title: The receiver's replacement Bank uses the same parent Q. Its local bank ID is 901. The example assumes no other bank allocations between these two instances.

g.aria-label: I04: complete the block and determine its shared block ID. Show explanation
g.title: I04: Both nodes determine the same block ID from the same complete block data and selected parent. This does not require matching bank IDs or a finality certificate.
g.text: I04 · Complete block data → shared block identity
The block ID can be computed without executing transactions.

g.aria-label: Completed block: slot 104, shared block ID H104, different local bank IDs. Show explanation
g.title: Completed block identity is (104, H104) on both nodes. In Alpenglow H104 is the double Merkle root over every FEC-set root plus a parent-information leaf. It is distinct from the execution bank hash. A block ID does not itself establish finality.
g.text: COMPLETE BLOCK · SAME ID ON BOTH NODES
These local bank IDs identify different objects for the same block.
Illustrative IDs: P, Q, and H104 stand for full cryptographic hashes.
Bank hash is a separate execution-state hash. Bank ID is only a local instance number.
